chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Some of our companions asked him about a Muslim man who is attracted to a beautiful woman, whether it is permissible for him to marry her while she is mad (mentally ill). He said, 'No. But if he has a female slave who is mad, there is no harm in him having intercourse with her, and he should not seek her offspring.'

key_terms.يَطْلُبَ وَلَدَهَا: To seek her offspring / procreate with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a mentally ill woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the legal capacity for marriage and sexual relations by ruling that a free, mentally ill woman is unsuitable for marriage due to the complexities of marital rights, whereas a female slave (umm walad) may be sexually approached without the obligation of seeking offspring. This ruling reflects the classical Shia juristic view that mental incapacity in free women precludes the full establishment of marital bonds, while in slaves, it primarily affects the lineage of children rather than the act of consummation itself. The distinction highlights the practical legal considerations regarding guardianship and progeny in pre-modern Islamic family law.
